title: Company Pulse AMA prep notes (scratch)
body:
Purpose / quick notes:
- Short, candid AMA to follow the monthly Company Pulse email (30–40 min). Goal = surface hard questions, reduce rumor, show decisions and trade-offs. Keep it pragmatic, not a product demo.
- Tone: transparent, operational, appreciative. Avoid overpromising timelines.

Event logistics (ops):
- Date/time: Tue Mar 16, 10:00 PT (confirm rooms + live stream).
- Format: 10m quick updates from Exec team (CEO, CTO, Head Product), 35m live Q&A + 5m close.
- Moderation: Marco to moderate live queue; I will triage Slack/Slido questions.
- Recording: yes; transcript + short FAQ doc published to Confluence same day.

High-level opening (CEO) — 2 min elevator:
- Quick state: revenue growth steady; platform availability 99.95% last 30d; new Dedicated customers onboarding ongoing.
- Why this AMA: recent product & infra shifts (routing policies, quantization experiments) generated questions — want to answer them directly.
- One ask: tell us one thing that surprised you since last pulse.

CTO talking points (3–4 min):
- Performance wins: p99 generation latency improved ~15% after kernel selection changes and batching tweaks; average per-token cost down ~8% vs Q4 baseline.
- Private deployments: first production VPC customer went live in Feb; initial feedback shows config friction around KMS policies — owners: infra + security.
- Reliability: two small SRE incidents in Feb; SLO blameless postmortem in progress, short-term mitigations already rolled.
- What we need from teams: clear rollout owners for model swaps and one owner for each critical route.

Product / Head of Product (3 min):
- Roadmap highlights: hosted API streaming improvements, rollout flags for model versioning, rollout of Optimize recommendations in beta for select customers next quarter.
- Metrics to cite: API active keys +11% MoM; embedding requests steady; adoption of dedicated plans increased after pricing change.
- Customer asks we hear most: lower-latency tiers, quantized model quality regressions, better cost visibility per route.

Q&A: prioritized topics and suggested answers (scratch):
1) Question: "Are there hiring freezes?"
   Suggested answer: No broad freeze. We are prioritizing critical hires for infra, SRE, and select growth roles. We are taking a more conservative cadence for non-critical roles. (If asked for numbers: hiring cadence down ~20% vs last year; headcount still planned to grow but slower.)

2) Question: "Is there a pivot away from open models / community models?"
   Suggested answer: No. We continue to support curated open models in the catalog while investing in performance and operational features. The strategic focus is serving — not owning models.

3) Question: "Why did X route get downgraded to fallback yesterday?"
   Suggested answer: Short version: capacity mismatch + model variant regression risk. Long version: automated smart routing detected elevated token-latency on the preferred shard and failed over to alternative that preserved SLOs. Working on better signals so fallbacks are smoother. (Link to incident postmortem.)

4) Question: "What are we doing on cost-per-token?"
   Suggested answer: Multiple levers: batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization profiles for eligible workloads, intelligent fallback to cheaper compatible variants. We have a pilot that cut unit cost ~12% for heavy conversational workloads.

5) Question: "Any changes to SLA or pricing for Dedicated customers?"
   Suggested answer: No immediate changes. We are offering clarified burst policies and some new tools for capacity predictions. Any contract changes will be communicated by Sales/CS directly.

6) Tough one: "Are we going to sell the company or take acquisition offers?"
   Suggested answer: No active process to sell. Leadership continuously evaluates strategic options, but nothing to announce. Focus remains on product + customers.

7) Question: "What about runway / funding?"
   Suggested answer: We closed Series C in 2024 and have sufficient runway for planned initiatives. Finance is tracking scenario models; we will share high-level cadence in next Quarterly Update.

Notes on handling hostile / repeated questions:
- Acknowledge, avoid repeating speculation. If question demands data we don’t want to share, pivot to what we will share publicly and offer to follow up offline.
- For product regressions: acknowledge impact, summarize investigation status, commit to a timeline for a follow-up update (e.g., 48–72 hours).

Moderator cheat sheet (Marco):
- Prioritize: reliability incidents, customer-impacting changes, hiring, product roadmaps.
- Use slido polls to rate signal: "Was this helpful?" and "Top topics we should deep dive next time".
- If live queue floods, pull top upvoted questions only and capture rest for follow-up doc.

Personal prep notes for presenters (Jasmin):
- Keep answers short (<90s) for live Q&A to get through more questions.
- Use 1 metric + 1 concrete example pattern to make answers tangible.
- Bring 2 quick customer anecdotes (Dedicated onboarding success; a latency regression that triggered fallback) — anonymize as needed.

Post-event follow-ups:
- Publish recording + 1-page FAQ within same day. I will draft the FAQ; request execs to approve within 6 hours of event end.
- Tag relevant Confluence pages and link incident PMs.
- Collect feedback via short pulse survey (2 questions) and aggregate results for Execs.

Loose TODOs before event:
- Marco: confirm room & stream, set up Slido (Mar 11).
- Aisha: draft 1-pg FAQ template (Mar 12).
- CTO: 1 slide with p99 trend & recent mitigations (Mar 13).
- CEO: 2–3 line open + close (Mar 13).
- Me (Jasmin): finalize moderator plan + sample responses (Mar 14).

Open questions / unresolved:
- Do we want to allow anonymous questions? pros/cons listed below — need final call.
- Exact list of metrics to publish (p50/p90/p99, revenue growth %, active keys) — finalize with Finance.

Quick thinkpoints on anonymous Qs:
- Pros: higher honesty for sensitive topics.
- Cons: harder to follow up; potential for trolling.
- Compromise: allow anonymous upvotes but require user identity for follow-up.

Final note (scratch): keep this loose and iteratively refine. This doc is my working pad — expect edits from Marco and Aisha.

---
